title: papaver pyrenaicum aurantiacum
intro: Papaver pyrenaicum aurantiacum, commonly known as the Pyrenean poppy or golden poppy, is a flowering plant species in the family Papaveraceae. This plant is used in traditional medicine, valued for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which may help alleviate symptoms of pain, wounds, and infections. The therapeutic actions of Papaver pyrenaicum aurantiacum are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including alkaloids, glycosides, and flavonoids, which may exhibit analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antispasmodic effects. The plant's bioactive constituents, specifically the alkaloid chelidonine, have been shown to exhibit potential therapeutic benefits, including pain relief and anti-inflammatory activity.
